key_findings.detail:
Superstrate thin-film Si modules have the glass cover **directly bonded to the TCO cell layer** — there is no encapsulant between the glass and the cell. The only encapsulant (typically ionomer) is on the back side. This means:

- Na⁺ from glass can reach the TCO directly with minimal resistance
- High-resistivity ionomer on the back cannot block Na⁺ migration (it is on the wrong side)
- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=1|Shioda et al. (2017), p.1]]

Thin-film Si PID follows a two-phase progression, unlike c-Si:

- **Phase 1 (0–150 h):** Isc and FF decrease and saturate; current initially flows primarily through surface pathways and causes interface weakening
- **Phase 2 (150–310 h):** Voc continues declining without saturation; progressive electrochemical attack deepens
- **Total power loss:** ~40% Pmax at 96 hours; complete degradation by 310 hours under −1000 V, 85°C, < 2% RH
- **No shunt resistance reduction** — confirming delamination (not shunting) as the failure mode

- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=3|Shioda et al. (2017), p.3]]

Two types of delamination form:

1. **Linear-shape delamination:** Grows uniformly from scribe lines (P1, P2, P3 scribes) across the module width; found after first PID stress cycle; irreversible once formed
2. **Spot-shape delamination:** ~200 µm diameter spots at the TCO/thin-film Si interface; appear predominantly after the second −1000 V stress cycle (following a +1000 V recovery cycle)

- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=4|Shioda et al. (2017), p.4]]

A striking feature of thin-film Si PID is that degradation **accelerates dramatically** after each recovery/stress cycle:

- **First −1000 V stress (300 h):** Gradual degradation to ~60% of initial Pmax
- **+1000 V recovery:** Complete recovery of all parameters
- **Second −1000 V stress:** Extreme rapid degradation — equivalent damage in only **36 hours** (vs. 250+ hours first cycle)
- Each cycle nucleates more delamination sites, making recovery increasingly difficult until linear delamination forms and recovery fails entirely

- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=5|Shioda et al. (2017), p.5]]

Modules after 5 years of outdoor exposure showed:

- Linear-shape delamination near the bottom Al frame (primary water vapor entry point)
- Delamination at junction box cutouts (secondary moisture penetration sites)
- Spot-shaped features matching laboratory observations

This confirms delamination as the dominant real-world failure mode in thin-film Si modules.

- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=6|Shioda et al. (2017), p.6]]
